stories.title: Healy-Rae will 'not be deterred' from work after assault
stories.summary: Independent TD Michael Healy-Rae has said he will not be deterred from his work as a TD after he was injured in an assault in Dublin yesterday. Mr Healy-Rae was assaulted by a lone man when his car was stopped in traffic on Cork Street in central Dublin, shortly after 4pm. He was taken from the road by gardaí who were quickly on the scene. They took him to Kevin Street Garda Station and an ambulance was called. He attended St Vincent's University Hospital for his injuries, and was discharged just before 9pm last night, having needed stitches for a head wound. The former minister of state had been in Leinster House earlier and was on his way home when the incident occurred.

stories.title: Cost of MetroLink project could rise as high as €17.5bn
stories.summary: The minimum cost of building a metro for Dublin has more than doubled in four years, with the estimated price tag now between €14.4bn and €17.5bn. The Government has approved the revised cost of MetroLink, allowing the project to fully go to tender, with a view to works beginning next year. It is one of the most significant milestones in the history of the project, which was first announced more than 25 years ago. When the Government applied for planning permission for MetroLink in 2022, it said the predicted price tag was around €9.5bn, based on a range of between €7.16bn and €12.25bn The new estimated cost now ranges from €14.4bn to €17.5bn with the expected centre point of €15.75bn. MetroLink says that building inflation and design changes have led to the increased bill.

stories.title: Government must make 'trade offs' for Budget - Chambers
stories.summary: Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers is to warn his Cabinet colleagues that they will have to make trade offs as the Government moves to moderate spending in Budget 2027 amid global uncertainty over the war in Iran. Ahead of next month's budget announcement, Mr Chambers is expected to tell ministers that they must "prioritise and make choices and trade offs for 2027". He will say expenditure will increase by €7 billion next year, representing a 6% increase on 2025, but still a moderation on the spending increases of recent years. The reminder for his fellow ministers comes with budget preparations intensifying as the Dáil resumes from its summer break later today. It is unclear how the warning will be received by ministers amid some friction earlier this year when the Fianna Fáil deputy leader announced spending curbs and introduced levies for each department to pay for cost overruns in the Department of Education. The move comes as the Coalition mulls on whether to extend excise cuts on petrol and diesel due to be unwound from 1 November.

stories.title: Next nudges up its full year profit guidance again
stories.summary: Clothing retailer Next has today edged up its annual forecast, as it reported a 10.5% profit rise for its first half, but expects sales growth to slow in its second half and warned of headwinds in its core UK market. The group trades from more than 800 stores in the UK and Ireland, including Reiss, Joules and FatFace outlets and has an online operation serving the UK and overseas markets. It said today that full price sales were 7.7% higher in the six months to August 1, helped by a hot summer in Britain. But it said full price sales growth would slow to 5.8% in its second half, and moderated its second half sales growth expectations for the UK to 2% from 2.8%, flagging concerns in its home market which accounts for about three quarters of sales. "Our primary concerns are rising inflation, higher mortgage interest costs and a weak employment market. These worries will only be compounded if they are accompanied by tax increases," it said in reference to new finance minister John Healey's first budget on October 28. "It seems likely that it (the UK government) will have to increase taxes in order to fund its expenditure."

stories.title: EU proposes ban on social media access for under 13s
stories.summary: The European Commission has proposed a ban on social media access for under 13s, with "safe design" obligations for platforms for users between the ages of 15 and 18. In her State of the Union address, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said it was "time for Europe to Act". She said the proposed Kids Act will have a "gradual and differentiated approach". Under the new rules, social access would be banned for those under the age of 13. Ms von der Leyen said: "That means only mini accounts from 13 to under 15, set up and supervised by parents, with limited features and time restriction. And between 15 and 18, safe design will be an obligation for the platforms." She said the EU had looked at Australia, which became the first country to implement a minimum age for social media use.

stories.title: Carrick shoulders blame for United's Carabao Cup collapse
stories.summary: Michael Carrick took responsibility for Manchester United's embarrassing Carabao Cup collapse to Brighton and demanded a reaction after his side were booed off the pitch at Old Trafford. An evening that began with teenager Shea Lacey marking his first senior start with a dream goal and Mason Mount adding a second in the 10th minute ended in furious fans unloading at full-time. stories.title: O'Shea and Manley to lead Ireland teams for shinty games
stories.summary:
Eamon O'Shea and Ger Manley will head up the management teams for the 2026 shinty-hurling/camogie internationals. Male and female sides will take on their Scottish counterparts in the hybrid sport, in a double-header at SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh on Saturday, 24 October. The women's shinty-camogie international will begin at 4pm, before the men’s shinty-hurling clash takes place at 6pm. Former Tipperary senior hurling manager O’Shea will take charge of the men’s team. He'll be assisted by Tipp All-Ireland winner Tommy Dunne, with John Considine, Seamas 'Cheddar’ Plunkett, Patrick Hannon and Conor Hayes rounding out the management ticket. Manley, who guided Cork to All-Ireland senior camogie glory in August, will manage the women's team. The Inniscarra native, who previously represented Ireland as a player, also steered the camogie team to victory in Inverness in 2025. His management team comprises: Gemma O’Connor, Elaine Dowds,
Jennifer Mehigan, Kieran McCarthy and Pat O’Neill.

stories.title: Messi named in Argentina squad for farewell appearance
stories.summary: Lionel Messi is to make one final farewell appearance for Argentina against Benin next month. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner,  who announced his retirement from international football after Argentina’s defeat in the World Cup final , has been invited to participate in the upcoming friendly on 6 October. The match in Buenos Aires is to be turned into a celebration of his career, with all his team-mates from Argentina’s triumphant 2022 World Cup squad invited. Messi has therefore been named in Lionel Scaloni’s squad for the upcoming international window, which also includes friendlies against Bolivia on 30 September and Burkina Faso on 3 October. He, along with midfielders Giovani Lo Celso and Rodrigo De Paul, will join the squad just for the Benin match. Argentinian FA president Claudio Tapia said in a video released on Instagram: "To all Argentina fans and Argentinians, I want to tell you that after a chat with the national team head coach, Lionel Scaloni, we have taken the decision to invite the best player in the world, emblem of our national team, our captain, Lionel Andres Messi, so he can have the farewell he truly deserves on October 6, here, in Argentina."

stories.title: Wall revitalised as Ireland target five wins this window
stories.summary: Ireland lock Dorothy Wall is injury-free and ready to hit the ground running as Ireland ramp up preparations for the WXV Global Series. The Tipperary woman featured in all five of Ireland's Six Nations games this year having made a successful return from injury, but now feels in a great place with a full pre-season under her belt. "Post-injury, I kind of went straight into a season, and having an actual pre-season to build up strength scores, explosiveness, etc, and to actually feel rested was kind of new for me. "I enjoyed that. I enjoyed the hard graft. I've really enjoyed getting more game stuff in in camp here, but it doesn't really feel like we've been out of the game either." Wall suffered an Achilles' tendon injury in the final Six Nations game of 2025, a 26-19 defeat away to Scotland. This meant she missed Ireland's Rugby World Cup tilt later that year but the 26-year-old insists she has no regrets. "I guess I can't regret an injury that wasn't my fault", she said.

stories.title: Caitríona Balfe wears Irish couture designs to TIFF
stories.summary: Outlander star Caitríona Balfe might have a globe-trotting career as an actress, but the Monaghan native can always be relied on to spotlight Irish design when she gets a chance. Balfe attended the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) this week, where she attended the premieres of two new projects: Tenzing, a biographical drama charting sherpa Tenzing Norgay's 1953 ascent of Mount Everest with New Zealand climber Edmund Hillary, and A Long Winter, an adaptation of the Colm Tóibín short story of the same name about a family preparing for a harsh winter in Canada. As a former runway and Victoria's Secret model, the star is no stranger to dazzling with her fashion choices, but it's clear that for this press run Balfe wanted to highlight Irish designers. Styled by Nicky Yates, Balfe first wore a stunning pale yellow gown by Standing Ground, the London-based brand founded by Irish couturier Michael Stewart, which recently became the talk of Paris Fashion Week after its sublime runway show. For the Tenzing premiere, Balfe chose a striking column-style dress with a high neckline, draping across the body and a subtle train at the back. The design also featured Stewart's unique beading technique at the waist. She finished her look with simple diamond earrings. For her next premiere, Balfe once again chose Irish design, this time opting for an opulent outfit by Dior by Derry designer Jonathan Anderson.

stories.title: US federal probe targets multi-million dollar Irish scam gang
stories.summary: Victims have collectively paid the gang tens of millions of dollars, according to US police investigating their operation. Some individual victims are believed to have lost several hundred thousand dollars. Police in the Pacific Northwest say they have identified around 30 people suspected of involvement in the scam, most of them Irish men who travelled to the US from Ireland. In the city of Seattle alone, police estimate victims have lost around $15 million. They include elderly homeowners who have lost life savings and retirement funds. The scammers, who have been covered extensively by Seattle-based 'King 5' TV's investigations team in recent months, also defrauded homeowners in the wider Washington State area and in Oregon. Police in the city of Seattle told Prime Time they have pictures and surveillance video of 30 people linked to the gang from the Pacific Northwest region alone. They say the majority of the suspects are Irish men who have come over from Ireland, and not second or third-generation Irish Americans.

stories.title: Ex-garda sentenced for sending friend PULSE data of women
stories.summary: Disgraced former garda Shane Flanagan engaged in "repeated criminality" by supplying PULSE identification data on 14 female motorists in Co Clare to a friend so the friend could view the women's profile photos on Facebook. At Ennis Circuit Court, Judge Francis Comerford imposed a sentence of nine months on Shane Flanagan, 41, of Ennis, Co Clare to run consecutive to the seven-year term Flanagan received in July 2025 for inciting strangers to rape a female colleague. Judge Comerford said that it was a "very serious offence for Mr Flanagan to disclose PULSE information during the course of his duties" between January and September 2020 to his friend, Colm Meere, 45, of Knockanean, Tulla Rd, Ennis. Judge Comerford said that "a garda's role is to protect society and women in society" but Flanagan had engaged in "repeated criminality" in providing the PULSE data on the women concerned. Judge Comerford imposed a 14-month suspended prison term on Meere who pleaded guilty to inciting Flanagan to give out the unauthorised PULSE data. Flanagan - appearing in court via video-link from the Midlands Prison - and Meere had pleaded guilty to sample counts concerning the unauthorised disclosure of PULSE date on 14 female motorists between January and September 2020.

stories.title: Taoiseach, Sinn Féin clash in Irish unity debate
stories.summary: Taoiseach Micheál Martin has suggested Sinn Féin may set back the cause of Irish unity by aligning itself with Scottish and Welsh pro-independence parties. Mr Martin questioned whether Sinn Féin was on the right strategic track after the party yesterday signed a memorandum of understanding with the SNP and Plaid Cymru to put pressure on the UK government to call unity referendums in Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales. However, shortly after Mr Martin's comments, Sinn Féin vice president Michelle O'Neill said the Taoiseach "would need to catch up with the debate". While Sinn Féin TD Matt Carthy said the Taoiseach's "attempts to shut down any discussions on Irish unity" were "getting farcical". Along with Sinn Féin leader Mary Lou McDonald, the leaders of SNP and Plaid Cymru yesterday called on the British government to "prepare for, plan and facilitate constitutional change". The group, who met in their capacity as party leaders - rather than as officials in their respective governments, also stated their ambitions for partnership around the economy, energy and international co-operation.

stories.title: Why are the EU and Canada getting so friendly all of a sudden?
stories.summary: Analtsis: The unfolding diplomatic choreography between Canada and Europe includes associate membership, trade talks, summits and the Eurovision This week, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen made an unprecedented offer to Canadian prime minister Mark Carney, who was the guest of honour at her State of the European Union speech in Strasbourg. She told Carney that she wanted to make Canada "the first associate member of the EU." Carney was clearly delighted by the surprise announcement, even as some EU experts were left scratching their heads. Under its current rules, there is no such thing as "associate membership" of the EU, but this does not prevent the two sides from inventing a new kind of relationship that goes by that name. From the point of view of the EU treaties, there are currently only member states and non-member states (ie "third countries). Indeed, the whole experience of Brexit served to emphasize that there is a sharp distinction between members and non-members and, that by leaving the EU, the UK could no longer enjoy the rights of membership. Article 49 of the Treaty on European Union says that "any European State" that respects the values of the EU may apply to join. It is generally thought that Canada, being geographically outside Europe, is ineligible to join the EU, although even that is a matter of some debate. On the other hand, the EU could make use of a different provision of the treaties (Art 217) to negotiate an Association Agreement with Canada. The EU has Association Agreements with several countries, such as Ukraine. It is an open question whether being an "associate member" would give Canada special privileges, such as the right to participate in EU decision-making bodies. It also remains to be seen whether the prospect of associate membership might also be held out to other close EU allies, such as Norway or the post-Brexit UK.

stories.title: Houthis reject Saudi coalition charge of attack on Mecca
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthis have rejected as a "lie" a Saudi statement that it had shot down a drone heading towards Islam's holy city of Mecca, which attracts millions of pilgrims each year. The Saudi-led coalition battling the Houthis had accused them of targeting of Mecca, sparking outrage across the Muslim world. Fresh fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Yemen's Saudi-backed government has dragged in the kingdom, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on its ships in the Red Sea. Last week, the Houthis seized control of the entirety of Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital artery for Saudi oil exports as the wider Middle East war chokes off the Strait of Hormuz shipping route. "The claims about targeting Mecca are a worn-out lie that has been used before and no longer fools anyone," Hazem al-Assad from the Houthi politburo wrote on X. "I saw a few people panicking, running to the window to see what happened," a Mecca resident who asked for anonymity told AFP.

stories.title: Munster pair keen to show provincial form in Irish green
stories.summary: If team sheets were named on form alone, Munster would dominate Scott Bemand's thoughts following their interprovincial title success last month. Having now picked off eight wins on the bounce across the past two campaigns, with an average winning margin of 29 points; they are not shorn of talent bursting through the seams. Two players likely to get the chance to show their provincial form on a national level are forwards Jane Clohessy and Beth Buttimer. Heading into the autumn test window, the UL Bohemians team-mates have just one cap between them, but that looks destined to change in the coming weeks and months. For Clohessy, who made her Ireland debut in the 2025 Six Nations defeat to Scotland, it has been a rocky road back to contention. The daughter of Munster legend Peter, she missed out on selection for the Rugby World Cup later that year, and suffered two separate arm breaks during the Celtic Challenge, and again in Ireland training, to miss out on Six Nations game time. But she's back and in tip-top form, so much so that missed the interprovincial final win over Leinster is easily glossed over.

stories.title: Szoboszlai screamer seals Carabao Cup win over Spurs
stories.summary: Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo – whose futures appeared in doubt this summer – both scored as Liverpool booked their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 3-1 victory over Tottenham. The pair were two of last season's most maligned players but are among the best performers so far in this stuttering campaign which shows glimpses of catching fire only for it to be doused by performances like Saturday’s goalless draw with Fulham. There was even a confidence-boosting display from second-choice goalkeeper Giorgio Mamardashvili, whose quick reactions prevented three certain goals, after his quality had been questioned – his failure to deal with the corner from which Conor Gallager headed in was the one blemish. But with Andoni Iraola’s side weathering a storm towards the end, Dominik Szoboszlai came off the bench to spectacularly volley home from 25 yards. Tottenham, whose only goals this season have been in this competition after putting five past Championship side Charlton, remain winless against top-flight opposition as their miserable run at Anfield was extended to one win in 31 visits and none in 15 years. And if Mohammed Kudus, making his first start since January, continues to miss chances like the one from four yards with the score at 1-0 in the first half there is unlikely to be any improvement.

stories.title: O'Gara to stay with La Rochelle until 2031
stories.summary: Ronan O'Gara has officially ended speculation linking him with Leinster by agreeing to remain as head coach of French outfit La Rochelle until 2031. The former Munster out-half had been touted as a potential replacement for Leo Cullen, who will step away from Leinster at the end of the 2026/27 season. However, earlier this month it emerged that discussions between La Rochelle and O'Gara on a fresh contract had started and the club have now announced the news. O'Gara was appointed head coach of the Top 14 side in 2019 - taking sole charge in 2021 - and guided them to European Cup glory in 2022 and '23. "My family and I are very happy and proud to continue this adventure with Stade Rochelais," O'Gara told the club website. "We have lived through exceptional times and gone through more difficult times together. In each of them, I felt the confidence of the Club and the support of our supporters.

stories.title: Masters At Work and Annie Mac lead Cork Jazz Festival line-up
stories.summary: The line-up for the 2026 Guinness Cork Jazz Festival has been announced. The 48th festival will take place from Thursday, October 22 to Monday, October 26, with an eclectic programme covering jazz, house, soul, disco, hip-hop, R&B, blues, Afrobeat and electronic music. Acclaimed jazz-influenced electronic act Berlioz, the London-based project of Ted Jasper, will perform at the Cork Opera House, while New York house duo Masters At Work, comprising Kenny Dope and Louie Vega, will appear together in Cork for the first time, making their first joint appearance in Ireland in more than 20 years. Annie Mac will also make a rare Cork appearance for a DJ set, with support from Tara Kumar. Boney M featuring Maizie Williams will appear as part of a tour marking 50 years of the iconic disco group, while British saxophonist Courtney Pine will mark four decades in music with a Cork show. Elsewhere, Keyon Harrold and Marcus Strickland will perform The Music of John Coltrane & Miles Davis at The Everyman, celebrating a pair of jazz legends.

stories.summary: From Macklemore's "Free Palestine" remarks in New Jersey to his removal from the Loop Tour and the subsequent withdrawal of four acts, here is how the controversy developed. stories.title: Things to do in Dublin (September 18-20)
stories.summary: From Culture Night to the Dublin Fringe Festival, there is plenty happening across Dublin this weekend. A celebration of 10 years of Joanne Hynes x Dunnes Stores is coming to The Atrium at Trinity College Dublin this weekend. The Galway-born designer will celebrate her story with an exhibition that looks at an edit of those 10 years through a series of vignettes exploring different aspects of Hynes’ design language told via knitwear, embellished textiles, print and recurring motifs. Open from 10-5pm on Friday and Saturday. Free to attend. The 21st edition of Culture Night / Oíche Chultúir will take place on Friday, 18 September. Brought to you by the Arts Council, this is a national moment, celebrating culture, creativity and the arts across the country. Search the programme to find screenings, workshops, exhibitions, walking tours and much more near you. West Meath Gothic blends aerial dance, physical theatre and live electronic music in a haunting journey through loneliness, imagination and reinvention. Directed by Katie O'Halloran, written and performed by Kate Finegan, the show will take place at the Project Arts Centre until Saturday, 19 September. Tickets €18. Have you got a mate who's too shy to put themselves out there? Or maybe they're just sick of the apps? Pitch your mate and help them find true love or sit back and find love via the romantic medium of PowerPoint! Date My Mate is a two-hour event taking place in Drop Dead Twice on Saturday, 19 from 7pm - 9:30pm. Participants will have up to four minutes to pitch their friend to a room full of potential suitors. Think: green flags, red flags, fun facts, embarrassing photos (used lovingly). Tickets from €13.85. On Sunday, 20 September, Hen's Teeth will host a sober rave with an extensive art exhibition from 4:30pm - 9:30pm. Feast your eyes and enrich your mind with a variety of live and pre-created art displays from incredible artists showcasing their unique expressions. Celebrate the autumn equinox with a modern twist on an ancient tradition, with five incredible DJs and plenty of mocktails. Tickets €27.79.

stories.title: Canada and Europe 'stronger together', Carney tells EU
stories.summary: Canada Prime Minister Mark Carney has said his country and Europe are stronger together, a day after EU chief Ursula von der Leyen's proposal to make Canada an "associate member" of the bloc. Addressing the European Parliament in Strasbourg, Mr Carney said that Canada welcomes the proposal. Earlier, the European Commission said the proposal is not aimed against the United States, after President Donald Trump threatened trade ties over the plan. "As our president made clear yesterday, the proposed strengthening of our partnership with Canada is not against anyone else, but for our common strength," the commission's trade spokesperson Olof Gill said when asked about Mr Trump's threat. Ms von der Leyen's pitch comes as both Canada and the European Union seek to pivot away from an aggressive United States under Mr Trump's leadership. "I think it's laughable," Mr Trump told reporters when asked about the plan.

stories.title: Abortion wait rule may impact care for some, cttee told
stories.summary: Ireland's mandatory three-day wait rule in relation to termination of pregnancy may result in an inability for a small group of women to access abortion care, the Irish College of GPs (ICGP) has said. It said that a proposed legal change under a Private Members' Bill - the Health (Abolition of the Three Day Wait Rule) Amendment Bill 2026 - supports comprehensive clinical care, while considering a woman's individual needs and preferences. The College told the Oireachtas Committee on Health that it is imperative that the proposed amendment to the law supports the importance of a reflection period for women who require it. But it said the length of this reflection period should be responsive to a woman's needs and should be determined by the woman in consultation with her doctor, rather than being legally mandated. The Private Members' bill planned would remove the legally mandated three-day waiting period which currently exists, whereby a minimum of three days must elapse following a woman's initial consultation before she can commence a medical or surgical abortion. Dr Ciara McCarthy, the ICGP lead in Women's Health, said that it has 4,900 GPs in membership and there are currently 498 holders of termination of pregnancy services contracts in primary care.

stories.summary: All of Ireland's 14 MEPs have signed a European Parliament-wide open letter to Ursula von der Leyen calling on her to introduce new EU laws banning any trade between Europe and illegal Israeli settlements. The letter, which has been signed by more than 100 of the European Parliament's 720 MEPs, was published a day before the European Commission president's state of the union address tomorrow and is targeted at placing pressure on her to take action. In the letter, MEPs say in their view it is time to "finally bring forward a legislative proposals to ban EU trade with Israel's illegal settlements in the occupied territories". Referencing British foreign minister Ed Miliband's decision last week to support a similar move, the letter continued: "Our citizens demand action. While our credibility on the international stage has already been damaged through inaction, a legislative proposals will be a positive step in the right direction. "We therefore urge the European Commission to propose the necessary regulation." The open letter follows similar correspondence in July by 71 MEPs, and a separate call in June by 460 former member state prime ministers, European commissioners, government ministers, ambassadors, MEPs and senior EU officials for tougher action by EU in response to what is happening in Gaza and the West Bank.

stories.title: Wizz Air trims second-half planned capacity by 5%
stories.summary: Budget carrier Wizz Air said today it had cut winter capacity by 5%, joining rivals in scaling back growth plans amid the Iran war, although a stronger-than-expected summer prompted it to raise its near-term revenue outlook. The US-Iran war has triggered the airline industry's biggest cost shock since the Covid-19 pandemic. Latvian carrier airBaltic became the first European airline to file for bankruptcy earlier this week due to fallout from the conflict. While full-service airlines have generally proved more resilient than low-cost operators, whose business models depend on cheap fares, even major US airlines have reduced planned flight schedules as higher fuel prices threaten earnings. Wizz is among the better-positioned carriers, with liquidity of more than €2.2 billion and fuel hedging covering 80% of its requirements over the next 12 months at about half the current market price. The airline set out medium-term targets of €10 billion in revenue and a 10% margin on earnings before interest and tax by fiscal 2030. It plans to operate a fleet of 335 aircraft and carry 127 million passengers a year by that date. Wizz currently operates 269 aircraft and flew 69.7 million passengers in fiscal 2026.

stories.title: Kosovo ex-president jailed for 25 years for war crimes
stories.summary: Kosovo's former president Hashim Thaci has been sentenced to 25 years in prison by a tribunal in The Hague for war crimes, in a verdict that sparked shock and anger among many Kosovars. Judges found Thaci and three other former Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) leaders guilty of illegal arrests, torture, murder and cruel treatment of people during the 1998-1999 war for independence from Serbia. As leaders of the KLA, they were ruled responsible for murders, illegal detentions, torture and poor treatment by the KLA during, after and before the war. But among many Kosovo Albanians, Thaci and his co-defendants are still widely lauded as heroes of its independence movement - with thousands gathering in the Balkan nation's capital to watch the verdict on a large screen. As the verdict was delivered, silence settled over the attendees, leaving many visibly stunned after weeks of preparations by Thaci's supporters for a possible acquittal. The crowd quickly dispersed after the proceedings finished. "This process was not about justice, but politics," pensioner Tahir Bytyqi said.

stories.title: Boehly & Walter sell Chelsea shares to Clearlake Capital
stories.summary: Todd Boehly and Mark Walter have sold their stakes in Chelsea in a deal which sees Clearlake Capital take full control of the Premier League club. American billionaire businessmen Boehly and Walter were two of the investors who partnered with Clearlake to buy the club from Roman Abramovich in a sale mandated by the UK government in May 2022. Private equity company Clearlake had previously owned 61.5% of the club, with Boehly and Walter carving up the remaining shares with another investor, Hansjorg Wyss. A statement issued late on Wednesday night said: "Chelsea Football Club today announced affiliates of Clearlake Capital Group, LP ("Clearlake") will acquire the ownership interest of Todd Boehly. "Hansjorg Wyss will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group. "As part of the transition, Clearlake will also acquire Mark Walter's ownership interest and therefore acquire full control of the club."
